Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- Policy stance: The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continued balance‑sheet runoff, signaling a wait‑for‑confidence approach on inflation returning to 2%.
- SLOOS credit conditions: Large banks reported weaker C&I loan demand and tighter standards for CRE loans; foreign banks also reported tighter CRE standards. For households, auto loan standards tightened. In residential mortgages, standards were unchanged for government/GSE‑eligible loans but tightened across many non‑QM/jumbo segments. Banks cite the economic outlook, risk considerations, liquidity/capital positions, and supervisory factors among reasons for tightening.
- Implications: Restrictive credit supply and softer business loan demand add headwinds to investment and real estate—especially CRE—offsetting some of the otherwise solid macro data (strong job gains, low unemployment). This supports the FOMC’s cautious hold and continued QT, with vigilance on inflation and financial stability risks.

Net tone: Cautious, slightly less positive than before given tighter credit and weaker loan demand in SLOOS.
